newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NISSAN MOTOR BUYS 50 PCT AUTOMAKERS .
newsitem.headline: NISSAN MOTOR BUYS 50 PCT AUTOMAKERS .

text.p: South African carmaker Automakers Ltd said on Friday an agreement had been finalised between its majority shareholder Sankorp and Nissan Motor Co Ltd for the Japanese firm to acquire 50 percent of Automakers.

Sankorp will sell 92.5 million shares in Automakers, representing half the equity, to Nissan Motor with effect from July 1, 1997. Nissan Motor is to pay 360.75 million rand for the stake, or 390 cents per ordinary share.
Subject to the scheme becoming unconditional, Automakers shareholders will comprise Nissan Motor with 50.0 percent, Sankorp with 37.0, Mitsui & Co Ltd with 8.7 and Nissan Diesel Co Ltd with 4.3.
The listing of Automakers on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange will be terminated and minority shareholders will be a paid 411 cents a share in cash.
The deal is subject to shareholder and High Court approval.
Automakers first announced in January it planned to delist in a move to bring in an unnamed new shareholder.
Automakers produces over 40,000 Nissan-designed cars each year, along with about 17,000 Fiat Unos and some 2,000 Nissan Diesel trucks.
Nissan Motor's investment in the South African car market follows a decision by rival Toyota Motor Corp last October to buy a 27.8 percent stake in Toyota South Africa Ltd for 446 million rand.
Automakers shares were last trading at 390 cents.
